faq.q1: How do I pair my child's device?
faq.a1: Go to Add Child, generate a pairing code, then enter that code in the Child App on your child's device within the time shown.
faq.q2: Why does my child's status show as offline?
faq.a2: This usually means the device hasn't sent a heartbeat recently — check that the Child App has Battery Optimization disabled and Accessibility Service still enabled.
faq.q3: How do screen time limits work?
faq.a3: Limits you set are synced to the device and enforced even without an internet connection, using the last successfully synced policy.
faq.q4: Can I change my subscription plan?
faq.a4: Yes — go to Settings > Billing to see available plans and switch at any time.
faq.a5: We collect only aggregated usage summaries, never raw message content, photos, or keystrokes.

gap.referralAdminSummary: Admin referral figures (codes issued, sent, rewards, fraud rejections by reason) are exposed by no admin endpoint. `/referral/me` is a parent surface for one family; reading it here would be both wrong and a privacy regression.
gap.productAiMetrics: AI sessions, goals created and completed, and rewards redeemed are not in growth contract v1.0.
gap.cohortRetention: Retention is available per country as a snapshot; there is no cohort breakdown.
gap.refunds: Refunds are recorded in payment_transactions but the growth contract exposes no aggregate for them.
gap.activeChildren: There is no ACTIVE_CHILDREN KPI. `childrenAdded` is a daily flow, not a stock; using it as a stock drifts upward forever.
gap.activeParents: There is no parent-level activity signal. `dashboard-metrics` counts devices seen in the last 7 days and the families that own them — a device is not a person.
gap.familiesByCountry: Registered and active family counts exist platform-wide only, with no country split. `newRegistrations` is a daily flow, not a stock, and dividing the platform total between the two markets by any ratio available here would be a guess.
gap.subscriptionPlanMix: The database knows the plan tier and the billing period (monthly / annual), but no admin endpoint aggregates them. `activePaidSubscriptions` is a single number with no plan breakdown.
gap.pilotEnrollment: The pilot service writes invitations, cohorts and redemptions, but no controller exposes a read of them. Only the pilot's configuration is readable.
gap.safetyEvents: Safety incidents reach an operator today only as AI_SAFETY_INCIDENT alerts — one row per threshold breach, not a per-country count of events.

funnel.title: Funnel — impression to renewal
funnel.subtitle: Counts are families, not events: a family with three children crosses CHILD_ADDED once.
funnel.fromMeasurableTop: From the first step we measure (INSTALL)
funnel.monotonicityHint: A step outnumbering the one before it. Reported, never zeroed — usually an incomplete ad-platform import.
funnel.activationTitle: Activation — the metric the product lives or dies on
funnel.activationHint: A child — not a parent — completed a real goal and was actually rewarded. Families that reach this step stay.
funnel.timeToValueHint: Median gap between family creation and activation — median, not mean.

overview.currencyNote: Every money figure is shown in its own market's currency. There is no combined total, because that needs an exchange rate — a financial decision nobody has taken.
overview.noCombinedMoneyHint: Adding EGP to SAR without a declared rate is a lie. Pick a market to see its figures.

forecast.title: Quarterly forecast & targets

forecast.assumptionsHint: Assumptions are returned with every number derived from them, so you can disagree with the inputs rather than the output.
forecast.rateOutOfRange: A rate must be between 0 and 1.
forecast.modelNote: The model is a monthly roll-forward with constant leakage. It is not a survival model and will lean optimistic in the first quarter.

unitEconomics.sameCurrencyRule: Every ratio is computed inside one currency. Comparing Saudi LTV to Egyptian CAC is a meaningless number that looks very convincing.
